text: **An ensemble explores a defined set of possibilities**

pages.title: Simulation ensembles
text: **An ensemble explores a defined set of possibilities**

A simulation ensemble contains multiple runs that vary initial state, parameters, inputs, stochastic events or model structure. It can reveal how uncertainty affects a forecast. The ensemble is informative only to the extent that its variations represent plausible uncertainty for the intended question.
## Design the ensemble explicitly

Parameter draws should preserve known dependencies. Sampling growth rate and lag independently when the fitted estimates are strongly correlated can create implausible combinations. Structural alternatives should be documented separately from repeated stochastic runs of one model.
## Agreement needs interpretation

If every ensemble member uses the same incorrect observation model, a narrow distribution may still be wrong. An ensemble is not a substitute for independent validation. Weighting models by past performance also requires care when the deployment conditions differ from the evaluation data.

The proposed platform should retain the ensemble specification, random seeds where applicable and a summary of failed runs. Excluding numerical failures without explanation could bias the result toward easier cases. Reports should distinguish a range of scenarios from a calibrated probability interval. A scenario range becomes probabilistic only when the weighting and uncertainty assumptions justify that interpretation and have been evaluated for the intended use.

pages.title: Virtual experiments and counterfactuals
text: **Virtual experiments generate hypotheses for physical testing**

A virtual experiment changes an input or model assumption and examines the calculated consequence. Candidate uses include comparing observation schedules, exploring sensitivity to temperature histories or evaluating alternative optical configurations. These calculations can prioritize physical experiments, but they do not themselves demonstrate biological effectiveness.
## Counterfactuals require causal assumptions

A model trained on observational associations may not predict what happens when an input is deliberately changed. For example, an association between a site and a growth pattern does not imply that moving a plate to that site would cause the pattern. An intervention model needs a defensible account of the relevant mechanism and confounders.
## Keep scenarios tied to their assumptions

The report should identify what was changed, what remained fixed and whether the change lies within an evaluated range. A hypothetical environment should not be described as an observed exposure. An apparent benefit should be reported in the model's output units and accompanied by sensitivity to alternative assumptions.

For AMReye.AI, virtual experiments are a proposed research service and engineering aid. They should not recommend patient treatment or replace laboratory confirmation. A successful virtual study ends with a testable physical question, an experimental comparison or a clear statement that the available model cannot resolve the decision.

pages.title: Synthetic data for software development
text: **Synthetic data can test software behavior safely and reproducibly**

Synthetic records are useful for exercising interfaces, permissions, export formats and failure handling without exposing patient data. Artificial plate images can also test geometry and boundary measurement against known constructed shapes. The validity of such tests depends on the property being assessed.
## Match the generator to the test

A geometric image with a known circle can test a diameter calculation. It cannot establish how the algorithm handles genuine biological zone edges. A simulated missing observation can test an unavailable-value export, while it cannot reproduce every cause of a real acquisition failure.
## Make synthetic origin durable

Synthetic status should be stored in the record schema and preserved in every export. A visible label alone can disappear when an image is copied or a table is transformed. Dataset lineage should identify the generator, parameters and source material used to construct the asset.

The proposed public demonstration should use synthetic or appropriately authorized nonclinical examples with clear labels. Production and demonstration records require separate namespaces or equivalent controls so that a demonstration result cannot enter a clinical workflow accidentally. Reproducible synthetic tests complement physical and clinical evidence; their scope should be stated in the verification report.

pages.title: Synthetic data and training contamination
text: **Synthetic training data can introduce hidden dependence**

Synthetic augmentation may improve robustness when it represents plausible variation. It can also amplify a generator's biases or leak information from evaluation data. A large synthetic dataset derived from a few source plates does not create an equally large number of independent biological examples.
## Split by the originating biological unit

Training and evaluation separation should account for parent images, isolates, plates and acquisition sessions. If synthetic variants of a test image enter training, visual differences do not restore independence. The same concern applies when a generator was fitted using the intended evaluation collection.
## Measure the contribution on real data

An augmentation experiment should compare otherwise comparable models with and without the synthetic material. The decisive evaluation should include real held-out observations and relevant rare or difficult conditions. Improved performance on another synthetic collection may simply reflect shared generator assumptions.

The proposed data service should retain a synthetic fraction and origin report for each training release. A model trained with generated growth should not cite that growth as experimental confirmation of its own forecast. Synthetic data may support engineering efficiency, but claims about biological performance require an independent evidentiary basis.

pages.title: Model verification
text: **Verification asks whether the calculation was implemented correctly**

Model verification concerns the software and numerical solution. A solver can be implemented correctly while representing an inadequate biological model. Keeping verification distinct from validation makes failures easier to investigate and prevents a passing software test from being interpreted as proof of biological predictiveness.
## Proposed numerical checks

Simple cases with known solutions can test the implementation. For exponential growth with constant μ, a numerical solver can be compared with N₀ exp(μt). Spatial transport solvers can be challenged with relevant conservation properties, boundary conditions and grid refinement. The exact checks should follow the equations and numerical method selected.
## A failed run is a result state

The simulation service should detect nonconvergence, impossible values and exhausted resources. It should return a failed or incomplete status with diagnostics, rather than a partially calculated trajectory labelled successful. Recovery must preserve the original failure and identify any revised configuration.

Verification evidence should accompany each released model implementation. Changes to a solver, precision mode or acceleration library may require targeted rechecking even when the biological equations are unchanged. FDA's computational-model guidance provides a risk-informed credibility framework for relevant mechanistic models; it does not establish the credibility of this proposed platform. [R58]

pages.title: Biological model validation
text: **Validation asks whether the model is useful for the stated biology**

Biological model validation compares predictions with observations that can test the intended use. It should establish the conditions under which the model is sufficiently accurate and informative. A model validated for visible colony area is not thereby validated for viability, susceptibility category or patient outcome.
## Design the comparison before collecting the outcome

The study should specify organisms, assay conditions, observation schedules, forecast origins, horizons and reference quantities. It should also define how missing outcomes and failed simulations enter the analysis. Blinded or otherwise independent measurement can reduce the risk that reference assessment is influenced by the model's prediction.
## Preserve unsuccessful hypotheses

A model that fails under a particular condition can still provide useful knowledge about its domain. The appropriate response is to restrict the claim, improve the model or collect additional evidence. Retrospectively removing difficult cases without a justified eligibility rule would overstate performance.

No AMReye.AI predictive twin is presented here as biologically validated. The proposed programme should progress from controlled measurements to independent forecasting studies and then, only where justified, to a specific operational or clinical investigation. Evidence from unrelated engineering twins demonstrates methods, not microbiological validity.

pages.title: Sensitivity analysis
text: **Sensitivity analysis identifies what drives the answer**

Sensitivity analysis examines how a model output changes when an input or parameter changes. Local analysis studies behavior near a selected point. Global analysis explores variation across a defined range or distribution. The useful approach depends on nonlinearity, interactions and the uncertainty relevant to the decision.
## Choose a meaningful output and range

A sensitivity ranking for mean colony area may differ from one for time to a threshold. Parameter ranges should be justified; an arbitrary wide range can make one input appear dominant. Correlated parameters need joint treatment or a clearly stated approximation.
## Connect sensitivity to a research action

If timing uncertainty dominates an early forecast, improving clock records may be more useful than increasing image resolution. If a model is highly sensitive to an unobserved parameter, the next experiment should seek information about that parameter or test whether the model can be simplified.

Sensitivity is not the same as uncertainty: a highly influential parameter known precisely may contribute little predictive uncertainty. The proposed report should therefore present both input uncertainty and output sensitivity. This combination supports a rational choice of additional sensors, calibration effort and experimental conditions without assuming that more measurements always improve the result.

pages.title: Model transfer between laboratories
text: **Transfer requires evidence about the new laboratory**

A model developed at one laboratory may encounter different media, workflows, environmental conditions, imaging systems or populations elsewhere. Some differences can be corrected through calibration; others change the relationship between biological state and observation. The proposed transfer process should identify which type of change is present.
## Separate instrument calibration from biological adaptation

A reference target can help align spatial scale or illumination response. It cannot prove that an assay's biological behavior is equivalent across laboratories. Conversely, retraining a biological model should not be used to conceal an unstable optical system.
## Adaptation changes the model

If parameters or learned components are updated using local data, the adapted system needs a new version and an evaluation appropriate to the change. Performance measured before adaptation should not be presented as evidence for the revised system. A holdout or prospective period is needed to assess the local update fairly.

The platform should support a site-specific eligibility state. A capability may remain available for research while being unavailable for a more consequential use at a new site. This approach allows collaborative development without treating every deployment as automatically covered by evidence from the first laboratory.

pages.title: Computational infrastructure and scheduling
text: **Cloud computation should preserve scientific traceability**

The proposed cloud or Hive Mind layer can schedule simulations, retain model versions and support authorized collaboration. Compute scale may allow more ensemble members or more expensive models. It does not remove uncertainty in the input data or establish the biological validity of a model.
## A simulation is a reproducible job

Each job should record its inputs, model package, numerical settings, random seeds where applicable and execution status. Input references should resolve to immutable versions or content-addressed objects. The job result should include diagnostics and the scope of any approximation used to meet resource limits.
## Local operation needs a defined fallback

An instrument should retain essential capture and record functions during a cloud outage when its qualified workflow supports local operation. A queued simulation can remain pending; the interface should not suggest that a missing result is a negative biological finding.

Resource optimization should be evaluated against scientific accuracy. Reduced precision, a smaller ensemble or a surrogate model can change the output and should be recorded. The research service should show when a job was completed, partially completed or failed. A successful server response alone is insufficient evidence that the requested calculation met its numerical and scientific requirements.

pages.title: Human interpretation of a twin
text: **A useful twin interface makes uncertainty actionable**

The twin interface should help a reviewer understand what was measured, what was inferred and what remains unknown. Visual continuity is attractive, but a seamless animation can conceal the point at which observation stopped. The proposed display therefore uses explicit visual and textual distinctions between evidence classes.
## Proposed viewing behavior

Measured observations should appear at their actual acquisition times. Forecasts begin at a visible origin and use a different line style or shaded region. The last accepted observation, horizon and assumed conditions should remain visible when the user changes the time view or exports an image.
## Test understanding, not visual preference alone

Usability evaluation should ask users to identify the last real observation, distinguish an imputed value and recognize an expired forecast. It should include plate loss, delayed upload and disagreement scenarios. A visually appealing display that causes users to mistake simulation for measurement has failed an essential requirement.

The interface should offer a compact explanation with access to deeper technical detail. Experts may need model diagnostics, while routine reviewers need the permitted action and reason for abstention. Both views should derive from the same traceable record and preserve the same evidence boundaries.

pages.title: Simulation reports and provenance
text: **A simulation report must survive outside the application**

A report may be downloaded, printed or shared with an authorized collaborator. It therefore needs enough context to prevent the simulated output being mistaken for an experimental result after it leaves the original interface. A watermark alone is insufficient because the essential scientific meaning belongs in the content and structured data.
## Proposed report contract

The report should identify the plate record, simulation job, model version and issue time. It should state the question, output units, last actual observation, forecast horizon, assumptions and uncertainty definition. Figures should identify measured points and simulated regions in their captions.
## Corrections create linked reports

If an input record is corrected, a new simulation can be issued with a link to the superseded result. The original report should remain auditable and clearly marked when no longer suitable for use. A correction should not silently rewrite the evidence that a collaborator previously reviewed.

Machine-readable exports should carry the same status fields as the human-readable report. Empty, unavailable, imputed and simulated values need distinct representations. This design supports later analysis without requiring downstream users to infer scientific status from a color, filename or free-text footnote.

pages.title: Research gates for predictive twins
text: **Advance the twin through questions that can be answered**

The predictive-twin programme should progress through evidence gates tied to specific functions. A functioning data pipeline is an important engineering achievement, but it is separate from a validated forecast. Each gate should define the decision, required evidence and consequence of failure.
## The first useful milestone

A credible initial research milestone could be a reproducible forecast of a narrowly defined image-derived quantity over a short horizon under controlled conditions. The study should include a simple baseline, unsuccessful predictions and a clear distinction between measured and simulated values. Its success would support that specific capability, not a universal biological twin.

Subsequent work can investigate longer horizons, additional modalities and interrupted observation. Each extension changes the evidence question. A plate-loss simulation remains a conditional research continuation even if the same model performs well while observations are available.

The platform vision is a coordinated system of records, measurements, models and expert decisions. Its strength should come from making each connection testable. AMReye.AI can pursue ambitious simulation capabilities while keeping the current endpoint reader, proposed engineering and future predictive research clearly distinguishable.
